The State of the Jeffreys Penalty at One Point

Source: R/jfp_engine.R
jfp_state.Rd

Computes, at given coefficients, everything that the value, the gradient and the Hessian of the Jeffreys penalty \(\sum_b a_b\log|\tilde I_b|\) read: for each block its rows, its expected information, the Cholesky factor of that information, the whitened rows and the leverages.

Usage

jfp_state(spec, design, coef, blocks, emethod = NULL)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

coef

A named list of coefficient vectors.

blocks

A list of jfp_block() objects.

emethod

The method of distributions7::distrib_expected_hessian(), or NULL for the family's own closed form.

Value

An environment with the fields spec, design (refreshed at coef), coef, ev, params, npar, offs, nb (the number of coefficients), total (the length of \(u\)), joint (NULL, or what jfp_joint_rows() returns), E, emethod and blocks, each entry of the last carrying block, index (positions in \(u\)), rows, info, U, Z, G, logdet and ok.

Details

For a block \(b\) with rows \(\tilde V_{q,t}\), $$\tilde I_b = \sum_t w_t\sum_{q,r}\mathcal I_{qr}(\eta_t)\, \tilde V_{q,t}^\top\tilde V_{r,t},$$ where \(\mathcal I_{qr}\) is the family's expected information on the link scale, minus distributions7::distrib_expected_hessian(). With \(\tilde I_b = U^\top U\), the whitened rows are \(Z_q = \tilde V_q U^{-1}\) and the leverages are \(h_{qr,t} = Z_{q,t}Z_{r,t}^\top\).

The point is the joint vector \(u\) of statmod_full_information(). For a model without a structural term it is the stacked coefficients. For a model carrying a filter it is the coefficients followed by the filter's free parameters, and the derivative of every predictor in \(u\) is read from the forward recursion (jfp_joint_rows()); a block in an equation that the filter drives moves with the coefficients and is rejected in this phase. A model carrying a mixture over latent states is always rejected, because its expected information does not exist.

The derivatives of the expected information are computed at the first request and kept in the state, so that the value, the gradient and the Hessian at one point call the family once per order.

Where a block's information is not positive definite its entry carries ok = FALSE and a log-determinant of -Inf, and the gradient and the Hessian signal an error.

See also

jfp_value(), jfp_gradient(), jfp_hessian()
